name: Mozilla Corporation
subcategory: web browser (Firefox) and consumer privacy products
origin_detail: Established 3 Aug 2005 as a wholly owned, taxable, for-profit subsidiary of the non-profit Mozilla Foundation to handle revenue-generating operations; the Mozilla open-source project itself was started by Netscape Communications (corporate origin); HQ San Francisco
openness_notes: Firefox and Gecko are released under the OSI-approved Mozilla Public License, developed in the open, and the company is owned by a non-profit foundation with a public-benefit mission, so it rates 4 (OSI + non-profit/community governance). Commercial dependence on Google search royalties is the main constraint on independence, not licensing.

license_history.note: Inherited from the Netscape-started Mozilla project; detailed NPL/MPL 1.1/MPL 2.0 history not covered in fetched pages

risk_events: Extreme revenue concentration: Google supplied 86% ($585M) of 2024 revenue ($680M) via the Firefox default-search deal

US v. Google: DOJ-proposed remedies (2024) threatened default-search payments; Sep 2025 ruling barred exclusive deals for six years but allowed non-exclusive payments; Aug 2026 US authorities asked the appeals court to overturn that allowance
May 2025: shut down Pocket (acquired 2017) and Fakespot (acquired 2023) as unsustainable
CEO churn: Baker stepped down Feb 2024; interim Laura Chambers; Anthony Enzor-DeMeo CEO from Dec 2025 with an 'AI browser' strategy
robustness: Two decades of continuous operation and an endowment-like cash position (2024 revenue $680M vs expenses $588M), protected by non-profit ownership from acquisition. But it is financially fragile in a specific way: one counterparty (Google) and one court case determine most of its income, and its diversification attempts (Pocket, Fakespot) have been shut down.
physical_science_relevance: Low directly; Firefox and the MPL are part of the open web stack used in research. Mozilla's open-licence model (MPL) is a template for weak-copyleft licensing of scientific code.
openness_effect_assessment: Full openness plus non-profit governance made Mozilla durable and trusted, and let Firefox break Internet Explorer's dominance, but did not produce an independent business model: 81-95% of revenue has come from Google search royalties for most of its history. The openness is secure; the money is not.
key_takeaway: Mozilla is the archetype of maximum openness (level 4) with a non-profit parent: it cannot be bought or relicensed, and it has lasted 20+ years, yet its survival depends on payments from a dominant rival and on antitrust remedies. Openness guaranteed the mission's robustness but not financial independence.
